title: The Reading Room
brief: An explorable three.js study built as architectural visualization, not a game: a double-height scholar's library (~7 x 6 x 5.4 m, west-facing) with floor-to-ceiling walnut bookcases whose shelves are packed with hundreds of procedurally-generated book spines, a mezzanine gallery reached by a slim walnut-and-brass staircase, a rolling brass ladder leaning on the tall left wall, a deep forest-green leather wing chair with ottoman and side table arranged on a faded kilim, a partner's writing desk with a green-glass banker's lamp casting a real warm pool of light, a globe in a brass meridian, a fiddle-leaf fig and a gallery fern, and one tall round-headed arched window carrying the low afternoon sun long across the walnut floor. Everything is procedural geometry with procedural materials, no textures and no images: herringbone plank floor, coffered beam ceiling, tufted leather, turned legs, brass balusters, muntined glass. Soft realistic light — a cool hemisphere fill plus a warm low directional sun through the window with 2K PCF soft shadows, warm sconce and lamp point-lights, ACES tone mapping, and a faint additive dusty sunbeam with drifting motes. Drag to orbit and scroll to zoom (OrbitControls); tap one of four saved viewpoints (the desk, the mezzanine, the ladder wall, the window chair) to glide the camera there on an eased path, or press keys 1-4; press Walk for first-person WASD movement with pointer-lock mouse-look at eye height, clamped inside the room. Click any object for a floating callout naming its material, role and dimensions. Capped render loop; prefers-reduced-motion disables the drift and the eased glides (instant cuts).
da: Architectural viz in a scholar's-library register, deliberately distinct from the pale warm-apartment scene: rich walnut (#4A2F1E) everywhere in wood, deep forest-green (#2E4633) full-grain leather on the seating and desk pad, aged brass (#B08D4C) on the lamp, ladder, rails and hardware, cream / oxblood / ochre book spines in warm procedural rows, warm lime-plaster upper walls, and one low golden afternoon key through the arched window; ACES tone mapping, a soft dusty sunbeam, minimal parchment-and-brass floating glass UI; Cardo for inscriptional labels, Archivo for the interface.
